title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this sheet belongs to Grothendieck's notes on motives and Hodge theory (c. 1969–72). The neighbouring pages in the scan are unrelated Bourbaki 'Systèmes de racines' tribu material that was filed alongside it.

**Notation.**
- H^i(X, Q(0)) is the motive h^i(X) of a smooth projective complex variety X, with Tate twist 0.
- ξ is the integral Betti fibre functor, ξ(H^i(X,Q(0))) = H^i(X_top, Z).
- ξ_C = ξ ⊗_Z C is its complexification.
- ξ_{C,∞} is the de Rham fibre functor, H^i(X, Ω^•_X) (algebraic de Rham, hypercohomology).
- T_C is the 'torseur fondamental': the torsor of tensor isomorphisms between the two fibre functors ξ_C and ξ_{C,∞} over the motivic Galois group.

**Opening claim.** Over C one has a canonical point of this torsor: the comparison isomorphism. In modern terms this is the canonical complex point of the period torsor Isom^⊗(ω_B ⊗ C, ω_dR ⊗ C).

**Morphisms between motives.**
- A morphism H^i(X^n, Q(0)) → H^i(Y^n, Q(0)) is given by a correspondence ξ ∈ A^n(X×Y). The superscript n is the dimension of X, so ξ is a codimension-n cycle, i.e. a degree-0 correspondence, used via transposition.
- Its Betti realization is x ↦ pr_{2*}^{top}(pr_1^*(x) · P_top(ξ)).
- Its de Rham realization is x ↦ pr_{2*}^{alg}(pr_1^*(x) · P_alg(ξ)).
- P_alg is the algebraic de Rham cycle class and P_top the topological one, normalised by P_top(ξ) = (2iπ)^{-n} P_alg(ξ).

**What he wants to verify.** The canonical comparison isomorphism H^i(X_top, Z) ⊗ C ≅ H^i(X, Ω^•_X) (the 'Hodge–Grothendieck' comparison) should be functorial in the motive, i.e. compatible with the action of correspondences.

**The computation.**
- Substituting P_top = (2iπ)^{-n} P_alg into the Betti formula gives pr_{2*}^{top}(pr_1^*(x)(2iπ)^{-n} P_alg).
- The topological Gysin map pr_{2*} (integration over the n-dimensional fibre X) differs from the algebraic trace by a power of 2iπ. He writes pr_{2*}^{top} = (2iπ)^{n} pr_{2*}^{alg}.
- The two factors cancel, and the square (Betti realization ⊗ C, can, de Rham realization, can) commutes.
- In the de Rham line he first records a stray discrepancy, '= (1/2iπ)^n ξ_C(ξ)'.
- He then notes in the margin that the compatibility comes from the comparison between analytic and topological forms, i.e. integration of forms versus topological trace, 'avec changement de conv. analytique'.
- He ends with 'Ouf !'.

**Purpose.** This is the routine but essential check that the period comparison is a tensor-natural isomorphism of fibre functors on motives. That is exactly what is needed for the comparison to define a point of the torsor T_C, which is the foundation of the period torsor and Grothendieck's period conjecture.
errors: The 2iπ bookkeeping on the page is internally inconsistent. The de Rham row ends with '= (1/2iπ)^n ξ_C(ξ)', which would contradict compatibility. Compatibility holds only once the Gysin/trace normalisations (topological versus algebraic, a factor (2iπ)^{±dim X}) are taken into account. Grothendieck himself flags this in the margin note about changing analytic conventions.

The direction of the power in pr_{2*}^{top} = (2iπ)^{-n} pr_{2*}^{alg} depends on the convention for the trace H^{2n}_dR → C. With the standard convention (∫ of de Rham forms equals (2πi)^n times the algebraic trace), the sign of the exponent on the page may be reversed. The intended cancellation is nonetheless correct.
The lower-row target is written H^i(Y, Ω_X); it should be H^i(Y, Ω^•_Y).

ideas.what: Torsor of isomorphisms between the Betti⊗C and de Rham fibre functors on motives, with the comparison isomorphism as its canonical C-point ('torseur fondamental associé à C')
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor of the motivic Galois group; comparison isomorphism as a C-point of Isom^⊗(ω_B, ω_dR)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (via Saavedra Rivano 1972, Deligne 1989, Y. André); period conjecture attributed to Grothendieck by André
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's own published texts as far as I know. Appears in Saavedra Rivano's 'Catégories tannakiennes' and in André's account of Grothendieck's period conjecture.

ideas.what: Realization of a degree-0 correspondence ξ ∈ A^n(X×Y) via x ↦ pr_{2*}(pr_1^*x · cl(ξ)) in Betti and in de Rham cohomology
ideas.modern_name: Action of algebraic correspondences on Weil cohomologies (realization of Chow/Grothendieck motives)
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures talk (1969) uses correspondences; Manin 'Correspondences, motifs and monoidal transformations' 1968

ideas.what: Normalisation of cycle classes by (2iπ)^{-n} between de Rham and Betti, and compatibility of the comparison isomorphism with correspondences
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the Betti–de Rham comparison with cycle classes and Gysin maps (Tate twist normalisation)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) gives the comparison; normalisation details are in Deligne's Hodge II / Deligne–Milne–Ogus–Shih

missed.claim: Early manuscript evidence (c. 1969–72) that Grothendieck explicitly formulated the comparison isomorphism as a canonical point of a 'torseur fondamental' between the Betti and de Rham fibre functors on motives. This is a documentary trace of the period torsor behind 'Grothendieck's period conjecture', which in the literature is mostly known through second-hand attribution (André).
missed.quote: C, on a un objet canonique de ξ_C de T_C(Z) [T_C torseur fondamental associé à C]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution of the period-torsor viewpoint (Kontsevich–Zagier periods, André's motivic periods) to Grothendieck's own notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine normalisation check. Its historical interest is limited to being a manuscript witness of Grothendieck using the period torsor 'torseur fondamental', which is already attributed to him in the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'X^n', 'Y^n' indicate varieties of dimension n, so ξ ∈ A^n(X×Y) is a degree-0 correspondence; this is not a cartesian power.
'(pour X, i donnés)' should read 'Considérons l'isom can (pour X, i donnés)'.
'Cet isom [...] fonctoriel en H^i(X,Q(0))': 'fonctoriel' appears to be kept (underlined) rather than struck out; the intended reading is 'Cet isom. est fonctoriel en H^i(X,Q(0))'.
The lower-row target should be H^i(Y, Ω^•_Y); the manuscript appears to write Ω_X.
Marginal note reads approximately: 'Cette compatibilité provient de l'isom. formes analytiques et topologiques (avec changement de conv. analytique)'.
Under the de Rham arrow: 'ξ^b_{C,∞}(ξ) défini par P_alg(ξ) = (1/2iπ)^n ξ_C(ξ)'.
